key_insight: The thesis shows that in very large action spaces, sharing structure across actions is crucial for both online exploration and offline learning, enabling better sample efficiency and more stable policy optimization.
engineering_relevance: The methods are relevant for recommender systems, ad selection, and other decision engines where action sets are huge and feedback is sparse or logged.
method: meTS: a mixed-effect Thompson sampling method that shares statistical strength across actions for on-policy learning.
dTS: a diffusion-inspired structured prior for modeling dependencies between actions and improving regret in large action spaces.
sDM plus pessimistic off-policy objectives: latent-variable direct modeling and concave, efficiently optimizable policy-weighted likelihood / importance-sampling formulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regret guarantees for the on-policy methods and emphasizes optimization-vs-estimation trade-offs, bias-variance control, and PAC-Bayesian bounds in the off-policy setting.
watch_item: These approaches rely on structured assumptions and careful optimization; in practice, misspecified action dependencies or unstable importance weights can still hurt performance.
paper_title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces
